best_human.source: Mohannad Shehadeh, William Kingsford, and Frank R. Kschischang, New Difference Triangle Sets by a Field-Programmable Gate Array-Based Search Technique, Journal of Combinatorial Designs 34 (2026), 37-50; first published online 2025-10-02.
best_human.source_version: Version of record. Table 1 reports the new upper bound 112 for (n,k)=(7,5), improved from 113. Appendix A lists the construction.
best_human.ai_provenance: The paper does not report whether AI or LLM tools were used.
best_human.evidence_state: Exact repository witness replayed and independently checked: 7 rows, 6 marks per row, and 105 distinct positive differences. This verifies feasibility and value 112, not optimality.

best_public.evidence_state: The 112 witness is reproduced. The paper calls it an upper bound, not a proven optimum.

best_reproduced.ai_provenance: The source's AI provenance is not reported; this is a replay of the published traditional FPGA-search result.

source_unattributed_records.note: The result is attributed to FPGA-based search. The article does not report AI or LLM involvement.

lower_bound.source: James B. Shearer, Improved LP Lower Bounds for Difference Triangle Sets, Electronic Journal of Combinatorics 6 (1999), R31.
lower_bound.calculation: M(I,5) >= (91I+6)/6. At I=7 this is 643/6 = 107.166..., so the integer objective is at least 108.

known_interval.status: unresolved in the cited sources; 112 is not claimed optimal

T039-C01.survey_scope_note: Checked the 2026 primary article and its pinned public repository witness, plus Shearer's 1999 lower-bound paper, on 2026-11-06. This is not a proof that no later or unpublished result exists.
